source: The user's Claude Code plugin directory listing, pasted 2026-08-15. Verified status read directly from the badge on claude.com/plugins.
$why-this-file-exists: Plugin enable/disable state is managed by the desktop app and written to NO file on disk — ~/.claude/settings.json showed 25 enabled and 0 disabled while the app had ~115 loaded and several just disabled by hand. That curation, and the reasoning behind it, would be lost on any app reset, reinstall, or new machine. This file is the durable record.
$how-to-use: Once the GitHub repo safety scanner (examples/SCANNER-SPEC.md) reaches v1, run it against each `repo` below. Entries that pass become candidates for SKILLS/REGISTRY.json with audit_status 'audited' and a pinned SHA; entries that fail get 'rejected' with the finding recorded in SKILLS/AUDIT/<name>.md.
$scanner-coverage-limit: The scanner is static and never acquires a repo. For plugins that are only a .mcp.json pointing at a vendor-hosted server, there is almost nothing to scan — the behaviour is served at runtime and can change after any review. Those need the manual Phase 3/4 path in lenses/repo-audit.md (live tools/list diff, sandboxed observation) and are marked needs_runtime_audit below. Do not let a green static scan imply those are safe.

$not-locally-auditable: ~87 of these have NO source on this machine — twilio-developer-kit, zoominfo, auth0, honeycomb and others were confirmed absent from disk. Their skills are delivered from Anthropic's infrastructure at session start. Auditing them means fetching each vendor's upstream repository, not reading a local cache.
$state-is-not-on-disk: Enable/disable state lives in the desktop app, not in ~/.claude/settings.json. There is no local record of which of these are currently disabled — this file records the DECISION, not the live state. Re-verify against the app UI after any reinstall.

reconciliation.method: Full plugin directory listing pasted from the desktop app UI and checked entry by entry for the Disabled marker.
reconciliation.result: 59 of 60 non-verified third-party plugins confirmed disabled. One miss: Bright Data.
